title: Extract Superclass

solutions.title: One Bookable superclass, one method left alone
solutions.tradeoff: InstrumentRental and RoomBooking now depend on a shared Bookable base for identity, cost, and description structure, so a third kind of bookable thing either fits those same assumptions or forces a rethink of the base. lateFeeCents stays duplicated in both subclasses on purpose, which looks unfinished to a quick read of the diff.

reviewFocus: Does Bookable declare lateFeeCents anywhere, abstract or concrete? It should not - check whether the walkthrough argues this or just leaves it out silently.

Do InstrumentRental.lateFeeCents and RoomBooking.lateFeeCents return the same number for two items charging the same rate over the same overage? They should not - if they do, the two meanings got collapsed into one.

Bookable's shared fields (itemName, units, rateCentsPerUnit) - did the extraction invent this vocabulary, or does it silently keep one subclass's original field name and rename only the other to match?
Is bookingDescription() abstract on Bookable, or did the superclass end up with a default implementation neither subclass actually wants?

Compare the walkthrough's argument for is-a here against drill-07-05's Extract Class: does it name the concrete thing that would have to be true for a shared component (has-a) to be the better call, or does it just assert Extract Superclass is right?
